sections.h2: What does the Webster County Clerk's office in Dixon handle?
sections.html:
Everything on paper that touches land in the county passes through the Clerk's counter at the Webster County Courthouse, 25 US Highway 41-A South, Dixon, KY 42409. Doors are open Monday to Friday, 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Recordings, voter registration, marriage licenses, and title lien statements share the line 270-639-7006, vehicle registration answers at 270-639-7005, and the fax number is 270-639-7029.

The same office licenses vehicles, runs elections, issues notary bonds, and processes delinquent real estate taxes. For someone selling a house it matters three times: when the buyer's deed is recorded, when a paid-off mortgage needs its release put on the record, and when a bill misses the Sheriff's April 15 cutoff and lands at the Clerk with a lien attached.

The land records page says recorded instruments reach back to 1786, though the county itself dates from 1860. Disputes about records or fines go elsewhere: the courts answer at 270-639-9160 or 270-639-9300.

sections.h2: Which Webster County records can I read online?
sections.html:
All of them are free to view, a service that began August 1, 2010. Staff are still scanning and indexing older books, so coverage keeps growing. The Clerk's list of what can be viewed:

  • Deeds: every book from 1860 (Book 1) forward, plus deeds of partition for 1893 through 2017.
  • Mortgages from 1972 and encumbrances from 1974.
  • Plats, all current ones, with the oldest in the two Processioner books covering 1861 to 1912.
  • Wills and marriage records from 1860, and every fixture filing.
  • Miscellaneous records starting with Book 20 in 1939.

A link beside the land records leads to a delinquent tax lookup. Before listing, search your name in the index and confirm each paid mortgage shows a release. Then check for liens, lis pendens notices, and judgments, because a title examiner who finds an unreleased one late in the process can push a closing back.

sections.h2: What formatting does the Clerk require on a Webster County deed?
sections.html:
Webster County adopted the Property Records Industry Association layout rules on January 1, 2020, along with every other Kentucky county clerk. A document that misses them can be turned away at the counter.

  • White 20 lb paper, 8 1/2 by 11 preferred and 8 1/2 by 14 accepted, with no watermarks.
  • One-sided printing, no staples or binding, no raised seals, no highlighter.
  • A clear 3 inches at the top of page one for the recorder, and 1 inch margins elsewhere.
  • Black ink with dark blue signatures, 10-point Times New Roman or similar, at most 9 lines per inch.

Closing attorneys normally handle this, so sellers rarely meet the rules directly. They matter most when a family transfer is typed from a template.

sections.h2: What will recording a Webster County deed or mortgage release cost?
sections.html:
The Clerk's schedule has been in force since January 1, 2020. Each document carries a flat fee, and every page beyond five adds $3.00.

A mortgage recorded together with an assignment costs $126.00 for up to 30 pages. Phone the office for a total before you mail a packet.

sections.h2: What has to be inside a deed before the Webster County Clerk will file it?
sections.html:
Two Kentucky statutes govern the contents: KRS 382.135 and KRS 382.110. Both tell the clerk to refuse a deed that falls short. Filing happens where the land lies, or where most of it lies.

  • Grantor and grantee names in full, each with a mailing address.
  • The whole price, certified under oath before a notary by both sides. For a gift, the certificate says so and gives an estimated fair cash value.
  • The address where the bill for the transfer year should go.
  • Where the seller got title: book, page, and recording date of the earlier deed, or an explanation of the inheritance.

Land passing under a will or by intestacy needs one more paper. Before closing the estate, the personal representative files an affidavit with the clerk in each county holding land, listing the recipients and the value of each parcel. If a defective deed is recorded anyway, the filing still gives notice to others, though a title insurer may raise the flaw.

sections.h2: What is the Kentucky transfer tax on a Webster County sale?
sections.html:
Kentucky charges the seller 50 cents for every $500 of value, with partial blocks rounded up. The rule sits in KRS 142.050. Webster County's Clerk figures it from the deed, takes payment up front, and stamps the date and amount onto the deed.

Worked examples: $200,000 divides into 400 blocks, so the tax is $200. At the county's Census median value of $112,900, there are 226 blocks and the tax is $113. Collection happens once per transaction. Five percent stays with the Clerk, and the remainder goes quarterly to the county treasurer's general fund.

Among the exempt transfers are foreclosure deeds, deeds in lieu, divorce transfers, partitions, corrective deeds, deeds that only secure a debt, and parent to child gifts with nominal payment. With no stated price the tax follows the open-market estimate.

sections.h2: Who else in Dixon should a seller call besides the Clerk?
sections.html:
A sale touches several desks in the same courthouse. The PVA, at 270-639-7016, holds the assessment and parcel data and processes ownership changes for tax purposes. The Sheriff, at 270-639-5067, collects the current year's property tax. The Clerk, at 270-639-7006, records the deed and takes any older delinquent bills. A short round of calls before listing gives you three payoff or status answers in one trip.

The county's history is also a practical point. Webster County was formed in 1860 from parts of Henderson, Hopkins, and Union counties, and the deed index starts with Book 1 in 1860. For a very old chain of title, ask the Clerk where an earlier link should be searched. Six cities lie inside the county, Clay, Dixon, Providence, Sebree, Slaughters, and Wheatcroft, and all of them record deeds at this one office.

sections.h2: Which recording deadlines can affect a Webster County sale?
sections.html:
KRS 382.110 sets two clocks. A lender holding a deed in lieu of foreclosure has 45 days from signing to record it. Someone who receives a deed from a court-appointed commissioner has five business days. When you are the seller in one of these transactions, ask the other party for proof of filing before you consider the matter finished.

Other filings arrive too: a mortgage release to clear the old loan, an affidavit of descent that records who inherited, and releases of mechanic liens or lis pendens notices that otherwise cloud the title. After April 15 the Clerk also receives certificates of delinquency from the Sheriff, so request a payoff on any earlier year before you list.

Webster County has 4,923 households, 73.8 percent of them owner-occupied, and a median home value of $112,900 per Census QuickFacts. Houses that need repairs, were inherited, or carry liens often sell as-is for cash, and the recording steps are the same for those sales.

faqs.q: What is the best way to file a deed with the Webster County Clerk?
faqs.a: Bring or send it to 25 US Highway 41-A South in Dixon, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., after confirming the total at 270-639-7006.

faqs.q: What is the recording charge for a Webster County deed?
faqs.a: $50.00 for the deed, and $3.00 more for every page over five. A mortgage release is $46.00; a certified copy is $5.00.

faqs.q: How is transfer tax calculated for a Webster County house sale?
faqs.a: The seller owes 50 cents per $500 of value, rounded up. At $200,000 that is $200, paid to the Clerk before the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Is there free online access to Webster County deeds?
faqs.a: Yes. The Clerk's website offers free searches of deeds from 1860, mortgages from 1972, plats, wills, and a delinquent tax lookup.

faqs.q: How soon must a deed in lieu of foreclosure be recorded in Webster County?
faqs.a: Within 45 days of signing, per KRS 382.110. A commissioner's deed must be filed within five business days after the grantee receives it.
